tests.name: Every node answers on its management address
Each host runs the algorithm its name says, with BBR available everywhere
Hosts pace with fq, keep no cached metrics, and have buffers for 300 ms at 100 Mbit/s
The routers route each site's LAN across the WAN
wanem bridges r1 and r2 with offloads off, so its queues count real packets
The emulator starts at the lab defaults: 30 ms RTT, 100 Mbit/s, no loss, 1 x BDP
The measured RTT follows the setting from 0 to 300 ms
The bottleneck caps a single flow at its rate
Random loss is injected in each direction
Moving the RTT during a flow takes effect at once and the flow survives
Each flow runs the sender's algorithm and together they fill the bottleneck
The site B hosts send with their algorithms too
BBR takes most of a long, shallow-buffered link from CUBIC and Reno
In a deep buffer CUBIC fills the queue while BBR keeps it short
The routers' and wanem's links and the data bridges are always MTU 9000
At 1500 the largest unfragmentable packet is 1500 bytes, and TCP uses a 1448-byte MSS
At 9000 jumbo frames cross the WAN end to end and through the bottleneck
All three algorithms run at MTU 9000
The hosts' MTU survives a reboot
